destination.name: Mornington Peninsula
destination.tagline: A bay-and-ocean peninsula south of Melbourne with hot springs and vineyards
destination.description: The Mornington Peninsula lies south of Melbourne on the eastern side of Port Phillip Bay, about 40 km long and tapering to Point Nepean. The bay side has sheltered sandy beaches for families, while the ocean side is popular with surfers. Peninsula Hot Springs has mineral-rich thermal pools up to 50 C, and Arthurs Seat reaches 305 m with wide views from its summit road. Point Nepean has an old fort and quarantine station, and is where Prime Minister Harold Holt vanished while swimming in 1967.
whyVisit: Walk coastal cliffs and bay beaches

goodToKnow.title: Drive or ferry in
goodToKnow.detail: Public transport is limited beyond the main towns, so a car helps. The Sorrento-Queenscliff car ferry runs hourly, 7am-6pm.

goodToKnow.title: Pack a jacket in winter
goodToKnow.detail: Summer is busiest, but cold-season storms on the Bass Strait beaches are dramatic. Bring a jacket.

goodToKnow.title: Hot springs peak pricing
goodToKnow.detail: Peninsula Hot Springs charges peak-time prices and has had age limits, so check both before going with young children.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The peninsula is at its best and busiest in {months}, with sheltered bay beaches and surf.

notes: Hot springs under-5 rule was from an older guide, so the tip is worded to check. Ferry hours should be re-checked.
